new_result.scope: Exact rank-three A=RMR^T. After deleting one original coordinate of spectral leverage h<1, normalize residual frame U=R_I(I-r0r0^T)^(-1/2). If every residual leverage is <=1/2, then the full quadratic form has a continuous density with sup <=3e[(1-h)|det M|]^(-1/3). If sigma_min(M)>=s this is <=3e s^(-1)(1-h)^(-1/3).
new_result.proof_mechanism: Condition only on the original deleted coordinate; residual inputs stay independent. Apply the completed diffuse separable-phase theorem to the normalized residual rank-three frame. det Lambda=(1-h)det M. Use its uniform L1 characteristic envelope to average and retain continuity.

partner_result_applied.application: For the partner harmonic family at m=5, s=1 and alpha=sqrt(2/5), giving branch bounds <606.245 and <86.941, hence density <607. For m>=6 the new deletion-normalized theorem gives continuous density <12.946.

first_unpaid_implication.statement: In the exact-rank-three heavy-null chamber, close the simultaneous regime where exact-ray saddle energy is arbitrarily small and either 1-h is arbitrarily small or a deletion-normalized residual leverage exceeds 1/2, while preserving original-coordinate product structure and not paying a single tiny reciprocal minor prematurely.
